name: Mean Reversion

card.context: A swing trade against a short, unusually fast move, aimed at a return to a short average, held 1 to 5 sessions. Form A: a leader above its 200-day and 50-day, up 25% or more, flushed into support. Form B: an index or leveraged ETF stretched down in a fear spike. The short mirror: a stretched rally below the 200-day.
card.pattern: At least two of five stretch marks: a 2 ATR drop from the prior close, a close under the lower band, RSI(2) under 5, 3 or more straight down closes, or a 40% drawdown in 10 sessions after a blow-off; on 1.5x volume, into a level a buyer can lean on. Not a slow, controlled decline.
card.trigger: OTHER: the turn, not the falling price. Intraday after the washout, the first higher low and a reclaim of VWAP or of the prior day's low; or the next session's 5-minute opening-range high or first green 5-minute candle. Market order.
card.stop: A few cents under the flush low, or the turn day's low if that is lower; if it is more than about 3% away, size down or skip.
card.failure_mode: A second flush to a new low on heavier volume, or a bounce that stalls and closes weak on day one or two; a report-driven drop with no level to lean on keeps falling. The house stop sits about 1% away on these, and one next open in five is already under it.

lookalikes.tell: Count the burst boxes and measure the flush. A capitulation needs 3 of 5 burst boxes, a 2 ATR flush on 2x volume and 15% or more off the 10-session high, and is bought on the undercut and reclaim of the flush low; a mean-reversion leader flush needs only two of five stretch marks in a leader above its 200-day and 50-day, often one day's drop into a level, bought on the intraday turn.

Count the down days and the gaps. A parabolic long needs 3 to 5 straight down days with two gap downs, a gap down on the climax day, and a 40% fall or a 5 ATR stretch, and may sit under the 200-day; Bracco's one-day leader flush (FIGR, SNDK) with no multi-day burst is this card's form A.

Look at what was undercut and how fast it fell. A U&R undercuts a visible level after an ordinary dip and needs no volume; a mean-reversion flush is a 2 ATR drop or 3 down days on 1.5x volume. Bracco's MAU&R "rubber band longs" (IREN, NBIS off the 10-week) are the U&R family, not a flush.

Check the volume and the shape. A moving-average pullback drifts 2 to 8 sessions on light volume to a rising line with no single day over 2 ATR; a mean-reversion flush is the opposite, a 2 ATR day on heavy volume through the short averages.

Measure the day and the pullback. An Oops gaps under the prior day's low in an orderly pullback 3% to 12% off the high with an Oops-day range under 3 ATR and reclaims the prior close the same day; a mean-reversion flush is 2 ATR or more, often after 3 down days, and the turn may come the next session.

For the short mirror: look at the run. A parabolic short needs Bracco's burst (three up days, two gap ups, a gap up on the climax day) and may be above the 200-day; the mean-reversion short is a 3-day rally into a declining 20 or 50-day in a stock below its 200-day. IONQ's four-day 54% rally was the parabolic family, not this short.

Before the entry: fewer than two stretch marks (mr.stretch_count).
Before the entry: the news behind the drop is a real change in the business (mr.inv_business_change).
Before the entry: a report within 3 sessions (mr.earnings_window).
After the entry: a trade below the flush low is the stop (mr.inv_stop).
After the entry: a second flush to a new low on heavier volume (mr.inv_second_flush).
After the entry: the bounce stalls and closes weak on day one or two (mr.inv_stall).
After the entry: no close back above the flush day's high within 3 sessions, sell (mr.time_stop, pending D-019).
The short: a short above the 200-day that is not a parabolic short (mr.short_above_200).
mistakes: Buying the falling price instead of the turn (Bracco's Right Side of the V; StockCharts: RSI(2) "can be early").
Buying the first or second down day (Bracco, 2026-11-01).
Calling a slow grind a capitulation: no range or volume expansion (Bracco, 2026-03-08; the detector's falling-volume veto).
Treating a band tag as a signal (Bollinger).
Fading a strong trend (Raschke: ADX over 32 and rising; two failures at a level first).
Holding a snapback as if it were a trend, or trimming it at 3R that never comes (Bracco 1-3 days).
Averaging down or re-buying the next red day (A5; E56).
Getting whipped in and out on the same day (Bracco, 2026-08-02).
Trading it in illiquid or hard-to-borrow names (B23, D48).
Mistaking a business-changing collapse for a stretch (Bulkowski's dead-cat bounce).
Journaling a "Mean Reversion L/S" trade with no definition: today the tag has no card, no plan and no unit.

short_mirror.note: Recorded on this card (mr.short_setup, mr.short_trigger, mr.short_above_200): a stock below its 200-day SMA rallies hard into its declining 20 or 50-day (3+ straight up days, RSI(2) over 95 or a close 3 ATR over its 20-day, on a gap or range expansion); short the turn down, stop a few cents over the day's high (D47), target the 5 or 10-day, skip hard-to-borrow (D48). Above the 200-day only as a parabolic short (39). The scan's four short examples (UA, NUS, IOT, FMC) ran 7.1R to 29.2R; its failures (NFLX, IONQ) were an earnings gap and a parabolic run. Whether to teach it is D-001.

best_conditions: Longs: a fear spike in a market that was healthy (Bracco's overreaction in October 2025, indexes just off highs); the VIX rising fast toward 30; breadth oversold (MMTW, S5FD, T2108); a Monday after a weak Friday. Worse: bear markets, even above the 200-day (Alvarez 2020 and 2022; the below-200 versions lost heavily in 2020).

management.gap_open: a trim level the day opens past is taken at the open (F63)
management.gap_against: the first 30-minute low is the new stop; out if past 2R (B20)
management.overrides: Option 2 (8.5), recommended for this setup only: at least a third at the first test of the target average (the 20-day SMA or 20 EMA for longs), then a breakeven stop, then trail the rest (E52) if it turns into a trend; and the 3-session time stop. Not ours: Connors' no-stop exit at the 5-day SMA; Alvarez's 2 x ATR(10) stop and 3 x ATR(10) target; the detector's 2R and 3R targets.

failures.why: eight straight down closes (-21% after a +58% run) ended with a 2.2 ATR flush on 3x volume under the 50-day, RSI(2) 0, four marks; the turn day reclaimed the flush close and closed red; the stop (2.2%) was hit the next session. An eight-day slide through the 50-day on a stock that had just made a parabolic top is a broken leader, not a stretched one.

the short: a post-report gap up 24% in four days on 4.9x volume, 47% under the 200-day, RSI(2) 100; the short triggered and the stock never came back, climbing for a month. A report gap that changes the story is an earnings gap, not a stretched rally in a dead stock; the honest stop was also 4.9%.

the short: a 54% rally in four days on 4.2x volume to 7% under the 200-day, 5/5 marks; the short triggered with a 5.2% stop, was hit the next session, and the stock traded above $60 within five weeks. Fading a strong momentum burst; a four-day 54% move is the parabolic family.

a report flush of 3.2 ATR on 6x volume, 17.5% in three days after a +27% run, four marks; the turn day reclaimed and failed, 0.2R. The honest stop was 6.4%, double A13's guide, and a report-driven drop in a name still well under its high had no level to lean on.

five down days, -11.2% after +34%, a 2.4 ATR flush on 2.2x volume, 4/5 marks; the second session after the turn was the 2018-10-10 market break, a new low under the flush low on heavier volume; stopped at 296.28, then 278.35 inside 20 sessions.

four down days, -9.4% after +34%, a 2.6 ATR flush on 1.6x volume at the rising 50-day, 4/5 marks; day 1 closed 101.13 in its lower quarter while the index made a new low and closed under its 200-day; stopped, then 81.30 inside 20 sessions.

the short: 10.7% under the 200-day, four up days, +23.1% on a 2.4 ATR pop, 5/5 marks, stopped the next day at 36.19. The 50-day (31.17) was 10% under the price and rising: a stock climbing off its late-June low, not a dead stock popping into a declining average.

flush-day volume 1.4x the 50-day average; the rule needs 1.5x. Six down days drifting 8.3% through the rising 50-day on light volume: the pullback family, no volume climax. Stopped on day 3.

up 15% from the 63-day low before the slide; the rule needs 25%. A 2.1 ATR flush with 4/5 marks but no leader's run behind it: a stock rolling over from a top, 317.37 inside 20 sessions. Stopped the next day.
the flush closed 3.0% under the 200-day SMA (855.47): a below-200 flush that is not a parabolic long (2 marks, no burst), so B26 says watch only. Stopped on day 2.

conflicts: Sources on this card are cited by position in the dossier's section 11 list (S1 the rulebook and verdicts, S2 the Sunday Scans, S3 The Parabolic Short, S4 the brain KB, S5 the app code, S7 Kullamägi, S8 Stockbee, S9 Kell, S10 Raschke, S11 Bollinger, S12 Breitstein, S13 StockCharts on Connors, S16 Bulkowski, S20 Nagel, S22 Alvarez, S23 the dossier's own check), as the validator reads an unnumbered list.

One setup or a family: the dossier recommends one Mean Reversion setup with forms A and B and the short mirror, beside separate Capitulation (34) and Parabolic (38, 39) setups; dossier 34 proposes one unit "Capitulation (Parabolic Long)"; dossier 38 sends Bracco's one-day leader flush here. The register's default agrees with this card (D-002).

The trend filter: Connors and Stockbee trade only with the long-term trend (longs above the 200-day); Kullamägi's parabolic long and Bracco's index and rubber-band longs often happen below it; Alvarez dropped the filter. B26 sides with Connors except for parabolic longs; the index exception is D-009.

Stops: Connors uses none and Alvarez found stops did not help his systems; Kell, Bracco and Kullamägi use a tight stop at the day's extreme. A3 and D41 require a real stop. The dossier's check shows why the house stop hurts here (one next open in five already under it); the turn's low, sized down, is the card's answer (D-005).

Volume: Kell and Bracco want heavy, expanding volume at the low; Alvarez's test found low-volume setups did better. Different things measured: a capitulation day against a quiet three-day dip. The card requires 1.5x for the flush forms (D-006).

Entry: Connors buys the close; Alvarez prefers a limit below the close; Kullamägi, Bracco and Breitstein wait for the turn; StockCharts notes the signal is often early. The card waits for the turn (D-003).

Target: the 5-day SMA (Connors), the 9 EMA (Bracco, parabolics), the 10 and 20-day (Kullamägi), the 20 EMA (Kell). None uses R multiples; the house trims do. The card recommends Option 2, a sale into the first test of the 20-day (D-013).

Is it a trade at all: Kell says the daily Reversal Extension is often best avoided; Bracco says most traders should buy the later wedge pop; Stockbee watches but does not trade it. Bracco and Kullamägi trade it.
Bands: Bracco reads a close outside the band as a coming snapback; Bollinger says closes outside the bands are at first continuation signals. A mark, never the trigger.

Shorts above the 200-day: Kullamägi and Bracco short stretched stocks in uptrends (the parabolic short); Connors shorts only below the 200-day; Bracco's SOXL mean-reversion short (2026-04-26) would not qualify under B26 unless it met the burst (D-001).

The stretch measure: Bracco's % ATR move (formula not given; the app's ATR-over-the-50 is not Jeff Sun's ATR% multiple, which runs about twice the app's number on a stock 100% above its 50-day), RSI(2), the band, the old brain template's 3 ATR from the 20-day (unverified). The card counts them as stars (D-114); the scan found the count describes the stretch but does not predict the bounce.
The journal tag sits in the Intraday group while UCT's trades are 1 to 3 day swings with an intraday trigger (D-016). There is no card, no plan and no unit for the tag today.

The Model Book "Parabolic Long" card describes riding a parabola up, the opposite of the owner's B26 ruling (D-014). The capitulation detector's liquidity floor is $2 and $10,000 a day against B23 (D-004). The voice KB line "Win rate drops 15-20% in chop vs trend" has no source and is in the recall bank (D-010).

Measured context, not our setup: the naive short-term reversal factor (buy last month's losers) was strong for 60 years and has been flat since 1990 and negative since 2020 before costs; a fall alone no longer predicts a bounce, so the selection (trend, stretch, capitulation, support, the turn) has to carry the edge.
The scan's ten examples: five of the extremes (LITE, KRYS, UA, NUS, IOT) were earnings reactions and the dossier's rules do not distinguish them; the owner may want a ruling.
